title: When Is an OIRI-Algebra a Banach Lattice? Structure Theorems and Counterexamples
summary: arXiv:2611.25083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the exact conditions under which a relatively uniformly complete semiprime $f$-algebra whose order ideals are ring ideals (an OIRI-algebra) admits a norm turning it into a Banach lattice or an AM-space. While recent literature claimed that this equivalence holds automatically in the presence of a weak order unit, we construct a concrete counterexample within a relatively uniformly complete vector lattice showing that this assertion fails in general. By analyzing the canonical embedding $\psi:A\rightarrow Orth(A)$, we prove that the equivalence between being an OIRI-algebra, admitting an AM-space or Banach lattice norm and satisfying $Orth(A)=$ $Stab(A)$ $=Z(A$) holds under the assumption that $\psi\left( A\right) $ is relatively uniformly closed in $Orth(A)$ (alongside a characterization via finite elements in the unitization $A^{\sharp}$). We also deduce immediate consequences for unital $f$-algebras and generalize our main theorem to non-semiprime $f$-algebras via the quotient modulo the nilpotent radical $N(A)$.

title: Weighted boundedness for the maximal operator associated with matrices
summary: arXiv:2603.02126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness on $L^p(w)$ of the maximal operator $M_{A^{-1}}$, defined by $M_{A^{-1}}f(x)=Mf(A^{-1}x)$, that is, the maximal of Hardy-Littlewood composed with a invertible matrix $A$. We present two different results of boundedness and provide a characterization for a particular case of matrices. The main novelty lies in examples illustrating the difference between the class of weights with a matrix, $\mathcal{A}_{A,p}$, and the classical Muckenhoupt weight class, $\mathcal{A}_{p}$. Finally, we extend these results to the fractional framework, considering the fractional maximal operator $M_{\alpha, A^{-1}}$.

title: Weighted bond posets and a new chromatic symmetric function
summary: arXiv:2608.08692v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical bond lattice of a graph was used in a formula of Whitney to compute the chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we use weighted versions of the bond lattice, to introduce and study a new polynomial and a new symmetric function invariant of a graph. Examples of the new polynomial invariant include the classical Narayana polynomials (for the path graph), the tree-Eulerian polynomials (for the complete graph), and the binomial-Eulerian polynomials (for the star graph). These examples suggest an interesting connection to $h$-polynomials of general graph-associahedra. We prove that for any chordal graph, our polynomial graph invariant is $\gamma$-positive. Multiweighted bond posets yield a symmetric function graph invariant that is an analog of the chromatic polynomial. The highest degree homogeneous component of this symmetric function is of particular interest. The parking function symmetric function introduced by Haiman arises as an example, as do symmetric functions studied by the first author in connection with multibracketed Lie algebras and with colored exterior algebras.
